$comment: What the template dev server answers at agentic-ui-config/bootstrap.json: the response the configuration servlet in nuxeo-agentic-core sends in production, with one fragment. On a server, these values are a bootstrap fragment in your own configuration package, contributed to org.nuxeo.agentic.ui.config; nothing is edited on the server. Everything here is public: it is read before sign-in.

content.$schema: Layer 0 bootstrap fragment for the template. Every key is optional; anything omitted keeps the value compiled into the application.
content.$nuxeoApiOrigin: Origin for Nuxeo REST calls, read once at startup and provided as NUXEO_API_ORIGIN. Empty keeps requests relative, which is correct behind `proxy.conf.json` under `nx serve` and for a same-origin production deployment. A cross-origin value needs CORS configured on Nuxeo — the stock Docker image sends no CORS headers, so a statically served bundle must sit behind a proxy instead.
content.$branding: Rendered by the shell and written to document.title. Change these two strings and reload — no rebuild.
content.$themes: Merged over the packaged themes by id. `tokens` are CSS custom properties written onto <html> by TemplateThemeService, so a rebrand genuinely needs no rebuild — edit a hex value below, reload, and the shell changes. The `--shell-*` names are the ones this template's own SCSS reads; a fork renames them to whatever its CSS uses. `base` names a compiled Material palette and is ignored by this template, which ships no Material.
content.$language-note: English only, on purpose. This template ships no catalogue directory and wires no TranslateModule, so listing fr and de here advertised two languages it could not render — in the public Layer 0 example a customer copies. Add a locale here only together with apps/nuxeo-satori-template/public/i18n/<locale>.json and the loader to read it; checkAdvertisedLocalesShip now fails this file if you do not.
